analysis:
Examined all supplied metadata, patches and BASE/HEAD workflow text against the canonical index and selected definitions. Changes concern artifact/toolchain integrity (A-011, A-017, T-013, T-034, T-054), not inference encryption, billing or live serving authorization. No concrete regression is established in this source scope.
.github/workflows/provider-release-cache.yml:76 selects qualification tooling for PRs and release tooling otherwise; runner routing, read-only permissions and credential-free checkout remain unchanged. Integration should verify that scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh and .github/actions/provider-release-build honor this distinction and that cache keys separate incompatible SDK/toolchain outputs. Cache scoping is asserted by a comment, not demonstrated here.
.github/workflows/provider-signing-validation.yml:57-60,136-139 replaces explicit SDK 27.0 checks with reviewed tooling's release preparation. Lines 89-93 now rely on its Swift wrapper for native builds and SDK selection. The separate signing job still checks out workflow tooling rather than candidate source, binds the artifact to this run/source/version, and retains runtime signing, entitlement validation, notarization and cleanup (125-234). No new candidate execution in the signing job is visible.
.github/workflows/release-provider.yml:112-114 selects release tooling globally; head line 1444 requires SDK 27.2 while adjacent source and bundle-digest assertions remain. Remaining material questions are whether the preparation script fails closed on unexpected Xcode/SDK versions, persists the intended wrapper/environment across steps without weakening signing-tool resolution, and produces consistent SDK identity/cache metadata across release and qualification lanes. Those implementations and the broader release workflow are not supplied; resolve these contracts in integration rather than treating their absence as a vulnerability. The toolchain change alone does not establish build qualification or alter TB-011 authorization.
